messages:
sre-bot: P1 alert -> runtime-crashloop-rate on cluster prod-eu :rotating_light:

sre-bot: Summary: multiple redwood-trt pods entering CrashLoopBackOff with SIGSEGV after model-accel daemonset rollout. Affected: redwood-trt:stable (image tag 2026-03-15), nodes impacted: node-7a,node-9b (approx 4 pods).

marta: saw the page at 02:03 UTC. initial spikes in 5xx from eu customers. grabbing logs.

yuki: logs show crash in trt_executor.so plugin: `SIGSEGV in trt_plugin_infer+0x65` followed by host kernel "segfault in user mode" messages. No OOM killer lines.

ken: nvidia-smi output on node-9b: GPUs show memory under pressure (~95% for a couple apps) but nothing killed. Could be bad pointer in TRT plugin when handling new attention mask shape from quantized model.

alex: Is there an active model rollout? I see model-accel daemonset v2.8 applied at 01:58 UTC. It installs a custom TensorRT plugin to accelerate attention.

marta: That matches timeline. Could be plugin compiled against a different CUDA ABI. Checking image build metadata.

yuki: Host kernel messages: `Mar 15 02:01 node-9b kernel: redwood-trt[2211]: segfault at 7f... rip trt_plugin_infer+0x65`

yuki: Also noticed `/var/log/messages` had repeated `nvidia: DRM: GPU reset` entries around 02:00. Might be driver firmware interaction.

ken: Quick mitigation: 1) scale down model-accel daemonset to prevent new plugin pods, 2) set runtime fallback -> cpu for critical inference route(s), 3) cordon nodes with repeated GPU resets.

marta: I'm going to set the critical route to CPU fallback via console routing: `route set /v1/generate -> runtime=cpu, fallback_timeout=2000` so requests don't hit GPU runtime while we triage.

alex: Doing scale down: `kubectl scale ds/model-accel -n infra --replicas=0` applied. Stopping daemonset rollout.

oncall-bot: @yuki acknowledged the incident.

yuki: After scaling down the ds, new pods are scheduled without the plugin and crashloops stop on new nodes. Existing crashloop pods still churn on node-7a/9b.

ken: I'll cordon node-9b and drain it. `kubectl cordon node-9b` then drain with `--ignore-daemonsets`. Evicting runtime pods.

marta: Customer ops: drafting status update: "We're investigating elevated 5xx errors for inference in EU. We've disabled a recent accelerator plugin rollout and enabled CPU fallback for critical routes. Further updates in 15 minutes."

alex: Patch attempt: rebuild of trt-plugin against CUDA 12.2 vs cluster running 12.1. Build mismatch found in artifact metadata. New plugin artifacts were tagged with cuda=12.2.

yuki: That seems root cause: plugin compiled for CUDA 12.2 ABI but nodes have 12.1 which leads to JIT issues in TRT and pointers into GPU driver memory being invalid -> SIGSEGV.

marta: For immediate recovery: revert runtime image to `redwood-trt:2026-03-10` (previous stable) for the runtime deployment using `kubectl set image deployment/redwood-trt runtime=registry:2026-03-10 --record`

alex: Applied rollback. New pods without the new plugin come up fine on healthy nodes. Crashloop count drops from 4 -> 0 after evictions.

ken: node-7a still shows GPU resets even with new pods evicted; planning reboot of host as next step if mods fail. Holding cordon.

yuki: quick host repair: reloaded nvidia modules and restarted containerd on both nodes; GPU resets stopped. Pushed a single canary runtime pod to node-7a, it stayed up for 10m.

marta: Good. Preparing incident summary for postmortem:
- timeline: 01:58 rollout ds model-accel v2.8 -> 02:03 crashloops + 5xx spike -> 02:10 disable ds + enable CPU fallback -> 02:20 rollback runtime image -> 02:35 hosts remediated (module reload) -> 02:45 recovery verified
- impact: ~12 minutes of elevated 5xx across EU region, ~0.8% of requests affected, highest latency spikes on long-running generation jobs
- root cause: accelerator plugin built against incompatible CUDA driver/ABI (cuda 12.2 artifact on 12.1 hosts) causing segfaults in TRT plugin and GPU resets
- mitigation: disable daemonset, route critical traffic to CPU runtime, rollback runtime image, cordon/drain nodes, reload nvidia modules, verify recovery

alex: Action items:
- yuki: add CI/build guard to ensure plugin artifacts record CUDA ABI and block promotion if mismatch (P0, 48h)
- ken: add host driver/firmware audit and auto-alert when GPU driver version mismatch across cluster (P1, 3d)
- marta: update runbook for accelerator daemonset rollouts to include preflight driver check (P1, 2d)
- alex: add metric to crashloop alert to capture GPU driver version and plugin artifact tag (P2, 1w)

oncall-bot: handoff -> next oncall is ken in 30m.

pagerduty: PagerDuty: ken acknowledged.

marta: Final customer impact note to status page: "We experienced a brief increase in 5xx errors in EU due to an incompatible accelerator plugin rollout. We've rolled back the change and applied host-level remediation. All systems are stable."

ken: Leaving nodes cordoned until we complete driver parity rollout. Monitoring for any regression for next 2 hours.

sre-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED by Marta @ 02:45 UTC. Root cause: CUDA ABI mismatch for TRT plugin; recovery: rollback + host module reload.
